raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
This feature is opt-in: `rollout.mask_stale_tokens` defaults to `false`. With the default or an explicit `false`, Trainer keeps the existing actor call and loss behavior. Enable per-token filtering explicitly:

```yaml
rollout:
  max_head_offpolicyness: 1
  mask_stale_tokens: true
```

Only token ages greater than the configured limit are masked; equality is retained. This switch does not alter rollout admission, scheduling, or cancellation.

Expired generated tokens can remain in completed multi-turn rollouts beyond the configured policy-version lag. Apply a next-token-aligned policy-version mask at actor update time, preserving fresh tokens, complete trajectory context, and rollout group membership.

The mask gates policy/distillation loss contributions and Megatron MTP loss. Keep the original reduction denominator, trajectory rewards, PRM scores, GAE boundaries, and advantage normalization semantics. Advantage normalization, when enabled, still includes original generated tokens; this change filters direct training contributions rather than removing trajectory history or changing credit assignment. Report version-filtered token fraction and post-filter version statistics alongside existing pre-filter metrics.

Validation: 252 CPU tests passed, 1 deselected across policy-version masking, diagnostics, MOPD, proximal approximation, rollout controller, staleness management, workflow filtering, and async task runner suites. Full pre-commit checks passed. Multi-node/GPU training and MTP integration were not run.

Opt-in follow-up validation: 150 tests passed across policy-version masking, the real Trainer training-loop toggle/default compatibility, diagnostics, MOPD, and proximal approximation. Full pre-commit checks passed again.

nodes.body: Could we add a pre-filter metric reporting the fraction of supervised tokens at each policy-version age? Define age as the current actor version minus the token’s generation version, exclude prompt and padding positions, and track invalid and future versions separately. Compute fractions from globally aggregated token counts.

@daihaowz Added this in 8d8d41ad. Before version filtering, `ppo_actor/update/version_stats/` now reports `age_0_fraction` through `age_16_fraction`, `age_gt_16_fraction`, `invalid_version_fraction`, and `future_version_fraction`. Age uses the next-token-aligned generation version; the original supervision mask excludes prompt and padding positions. All buckets share the globally aggregated supervised-token count as their denominator, so they sum to 1 for a nonempty population. The overflow bucket keeps metric cardinality fixed.

I added local, actor integration, and two-worker Gloo coverage. All 41 targeted tests and the full pre-commit suite passed.
Two MTP-specific correctness concerns when stale-token masking is enabled. Details are attached inline.

Align the MTP version mask with input-token positions

`policy_version_mask[i]` already describes the next-token target `input_ids[i + 1]`. Here it is passed to MCore as `loss_mask` with `labels=None`. MCore 0.19 shifts the mask once when deriving labels from `input_ids`, then again for the first MTP layer. As a result, the MTP target `input_ids[i + 2]` is gated by the version of `input_ids[i + 3]`.

For example, with tokens `[P0, P1, P2, S0, S1, F0, F1, F2]`, versions `[-1, -1, -1, 0, 0, 3, 3, 3]`, current version 3, and maximum lag 1, the resulting MTP mask still enables the expired target `S1`: its gate uses the fresh version of `F0`. This example does not depend on the pre-existing prompt-boundary alignment issue.

Please generate a separate input-token-aligned version mask for MTP from the raw `versions`, so MCore can shift it together with its targets.

Reference: [MCore label/mask rolling](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/core_v0.19.0/megatron/core/transformer/multi_token_prediction.py#L807-L857).

nodes.body:
Preserve the original MTP normalization denominator

In the reachable `calculate_per_token_loss=False` path, MCore computes `num_tokens` from this same mask and divides the auxiliary MTP loss by that count. Combining the masks therefore changes the denominator as well as the numerator, contrary to the stated requirement to preserve the original normalization.

For example, an original mask `0001111110` gives 6 supervised positions after MTP rolling, while a filtered mask `0000001110` gives 3. With an MTP coefficient of 0.1, each retained term changes from `0.1 / 6` to `0.1 / 3`, doubling its weight. The outer actor reduction retains the original mask and does not compensate for this MTP renormalization.

This path is used by Qwen3.5 with CP=1 in the pinned Bridge implementation; its provider only forces `calculate_per_token_loss=True` for CP>1. This finding is specifically about the False path, not a claim that the True path has the same amplification.

Please retain the original per-layer MTP token counts for normalization and apply the version mask only to the numerator.

References: [MCore normalization](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/core_v0.19.0/megatron/core/transformer/multi_token_prediction.py#L875-L892), [pinned Qwen3.5 provider](https://github.com/sitabulaixizawaluduo/Megatron-Bridge/blob/5d3268b972d55fe1d08b98b04e8c453467d4e51d/src/megatron/bridge/models/qwen_vl/qwen35_vl_provider.py).

nodes.body: With `rollout.mask_stale_tokens=True` and `enable_mtp_training=False`, `PPOActor._ppo_update` still adds `mtp_version_mask` to the batch. This field survives packing, but `MegatronEngine` only creates `mtp_loss_mask` when MTP training is enabled. As a result, a non-MTP Megatron run reaches this guard with `mtp_version_mask` present and `mtp_loss_mask` absent, causing the first actor update to raise `ValueError("MTP version filtering requires an MTP loss mask")` before the model forward.

+@contextmanager
+def _mtp_version_filtered_loss(
+    model: torch.nn.Module, input_version_mask: torch.Tensor | None
+):
+    """Filter MTP loss numerators without changing MCore's base-mask counts.
+
+    Qwen's bridge can replace packed offsets before GPTModel._postprocess, so
+    capture them there instead of rolling with the outer forward's metadata.
+    """
+    if input_version_mask is None:
+        yield
+        return
+
+    language_model = _unwrap_language_model(model)
+    original_postprocess = language_model._postprocess
+    previous_postprocess = language_model.__dict__.get("_postprocess")
+
+    def filtered_postprocess(*args, **kwargs):
+        base_mask = kwargs.get("loss_mask")
+        if base_mask is None or base_mask.shape != input_version_mask.shape:
+            raise ValueError(
+                "MTP version mask must match the model's final loss mask layout, "
+                f"got {input_version_mask.shape} and "
+                f"{None if base_mask is None else base_mask.shape}."
+            )
+        if kwargs.get("labels") is not None:
+            raise ValueError("MTP version filtering requires input-derived labels")
+
+        original_loss = language_model.compute_language_model_loss
+        previous_loss = language_model.__dict__.get("compute_language_model_loss")
+        mask = input_version_mask
+        layer_index = 0
+        packed_seq_params = kwargs.get("packed_seq_params")
+        cp_group = language_model.pg_collection.cp
+
+        def filtered_loss(labels, logits):
+            nonlocal mask, layer_index
+            # MCore rolls input_ids to labels once, then rolls labels for each
+            # MTP layer. Mirror those rolls with the same CP/THD metadata.
+            for _ in range(2 if layer_index == 0 else 1):
+                mask, _ = roll_tensor(

+                    shifts=-1,
+                    dims=-1,
+                    cp_group=cp_group,
+                    packed_seq_params=packed_seq_params,

+            layer_index += 1
+            per_token_loss = original_loss(labels, logits)
+            if per_token_loss.shape != mask.shape:

+                    f"{per_token_loss.shape} and {mask.shape}."

+            return per_token_loss * mask.to(per_token_loss.dtype)
+
+        language_model.compute_language_model_loss = filtered_loss
+        try:
+            return original_postprocess(*args, **kwargs)
+        finally:
+            if previous_loss is None:
+                language_model.__dict__.pop("compute_language_model_loss", None)
+            else:

+
+    language_model._postprocess = filtered_postprocess
+    try:
+        yield
+    finally:
+        if previous_postprocess is None:

+def _policy_version_loss_mask(
+    versions: torch.Tensor | None,

+def _log_policy_version_age_distribution(
+    versions: torch.Tensor,
+    current_version: int,

+) -> None:
+    """Report pre-filter token fractions by checkpoint age across workers.

+

inline_comments.body:
Align the MTP version mask with input-token positions

`policy_version_mask[i]` already describes the next-token target `input_ids[i + 1]`. Here it is passed to MCore as `loss_mask` with `labels=None`. MCore 0.19 shifts the mask once when deriving labels from `input_ids`, then again for the first MTP layer. As a result, the MTP target `input_ids[i + 2]` is gated by the version of `input_ids[i + 3]`.

For example, with tokens `[P0, P1, P2, S0, S1, F0, F1, F2]`, versions `[-1, -1, -1, 0, 0, 3, 3, 3]`, current version 3, and maximum lag 1, the resulting MTP mask still enables the expired target `S1`: its gate uses the fresh version of `F0`. This example does not depend on the pre-existing prompt-boundary alignment issue.

Please generate a separate input-token-aligned version mask for MTP from the raw `versions`, so MCore can shift it together with its targets.

Reference: [MCore label/mask rolling](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/core_v0.19.0/megatron/core/transformer/multi_token_prediction.py#L807-L857).

inline_comments.body:
Preserve the original MTP normalization denominator

In the reachable `calculate_per_token_loss=False` path, MCore computes `num_tokens` from this same mask and divides the auxiliary MTP loss by that count. Combining the masks therefore changes the denominator as well as the numerator, contrary to the stated requirement to preserve the original normalization.

For example, an original mask `0001111110` gives 6 supervised positions after MTP rolling, while a filtered mask `0000001110` gives 3. With an MTP coefficient of 0.1, each retained term changes from `0.1 / 6` to `0.1 / 3`, doubling its weight. The outer actor reduction retains the original mask and does not compensate for this MTP renormalization.

This path is used by Qwen3.5 with CP=1 in the pinned Bridge implementation; its provider only forces `calculate_per_token_loss=True` for CP>1. This finding is specifically about the False path, not a claim that the True path has the same amplification.

Please retain the original per-layer MTP token counts for normalization and apply the version mask only to the numerator.

References: [MCore normalization](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/core_v0.19.0/megatron/core/transformer/multi_token_prediction.py#L875-L892), [pinned Qwen3.5 provider](https://github.com/sitabulaixizawaluduo/Megatron-Bridge/blob/5d3268b972d55fe1d08b98b04e8c453467d4e51d/src/megatron/bridge/models/qwen_vl/qwen35_vl_provider.py).

issue_comments.body: Could we add a pre-filter metric reporting the fraction of supervised tokens at each policy-version age? Define age as the current actor version minus the token’s generation version, exclude prompt and padding positions, and track invalid and future versions separately. Compute fractions from globally aggregated token counts.

@daihaowz Added this in 8d8d41ad. Before version filtering, `ppo_actor/update/version_stats/` now reports `age_0_fraction` through `age_16_fraction`, `age_gt_16_fraction`, `invalid_version_fraction`, and `future_version_fraction`. Age uses the next-token-aligned generation version; the original supervision mask excludes prompt and padding positions. All buckets share the globally aggregated supervised-token count as their denominator, so they sum to 1 for a nonempty population. The overflow bucket keeps metric cardinality fixed.
